rationale: The provided excerpt from the 2016 NHTSA rulemaking (Federal Register PDF p. 6) directly states that the agency "has also been unable to directly measure the pedestrian and pedalcyclist crash rates per mile travelled ... because the Agency does not have data on VMT for HVs and EVs." The surrounding context on the same page confirms the use of a case-control analysis to compare crash experiences. This directly supports the claim that NHTSA stated this limitation and used a proxy/case-control analysis in its 2016 rulemaking. No alternative interpretation, primary counterevidence, or current-status change within the claim's stated scope (NHTSA's 2016 rulemaking) was found to defeat the claim.
evidence_locators: Federal Register PDF p. 6, NHTSA analysis of pedestrian/pedalcyclist crash rates and VMT
limitations: The review strictly adhered to the claim's scope, focusing on NHTSA's statements within its 2016 rulemaking. It did not search for or evaluate any current exposure-normalized U.S. studies on EV/ICE crash rates, as this falls outside the claim's historical scope and was explicitly excluded by the challenge instruction's 'Do not treat this older denominator limitation as proof that no such current data exist' guidance.
